# The elements in the video misbehave

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a row of the elements seen in the video, on a test bench, each set between
a small room and whatever is on its far side. Several things about these elements go wrong in this clip: in
their warning lights, in the way the element moves, and in what ends up on each side of a shut element.

Fix every problem you find in the clip that does not match the expected behavior below.

### Expected
- A shut element keeps what is on one side from reaching the other, and its warning says what kind of danger
  it is holding back.
- The warning only shows while the element is shut.
- A element shuts controlled.
- Every element of a element stays aligned with the rest of it.
- Everything else should keep looking and behaving as it does now.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

Inspect the attached video before making changes. You can pull individual frames out of it with
`ffmpeg`.

Space Station 14 is a remake of SS13 that runs on [Robust Toolbox](https://github.com/space-wizards/RobustToolbox), our homegrown engine written in C#. This is the primary repo for Space Station 14. To prevent people forking RobustToolbox, a "content" pack is loaded by the client and server. This content pack contains everything needed to play the game on one specific server. If you want to host or create content for SS14, this is the repo you need. It contains both RobustToolbox and the content pack for development of new content packs. ## Links
[Website](https://spacestation14.com/) | [Discord](https://discord.ss14.io/) | [Forum](https://forum.spacestation14.com/) | [Mastodon](https://mastodon.gamedev.place/@spacestation14) | [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/spacestation14) | [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1255460/Space_Station_14/) | [Standalone Download](https://spacestation14.com/about/nightlies/)

steps.message:
I fixed seven problems with the firelocks. Server and client both build, and the door, airlock, airtight and firelock integration tests pass (261 of 261).

One caveat first: `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` wasn't on disk (the folder is empty), so I couldn't watch the clip. I traced each expected behaviour through the firelock code, prototypes and sprites, and checked the sprite frames by decoding them with ffmpeg. Nothing has been checked in the running game.

**Gas getting through a shut firelock**
- `Content.Server/Atmos/EntitySystems/AirtightSystem.cs`: `SetAirblocked` only told the atmos system to recheck a tile when something *stopped* blocking air. When a firelock shut, atmos was never told, so gas kept flowing through it. It now rechecks on both closing and opening.
- `firelock.yml`, `FirelockEdge`: the door's picture and hitbox sit on the south edge of the tile, but it was blocking air on the north edge. I changed it to `South`, matching windoors, shuttle doors and edge windows.

**Warning lights**
- `SharedFirelockSystem.cs`: the warning visuals were never updated when the door changed state, so the pressure and temperature warnings stayed lit after it opened. They now update on every state change: cleared while the door isn't shut, and set from the current pressure and temperature readings while it is.
- `Server/Doors/Systems/FirelockSystem.cs`: the red point light also stayed on after opening. It is now switched off once the door isn't shut.
- `firelock.yml`, `FirelockGlass`: the glass firelock had no pressure or temperature warning sprites, so it couldn't show which danger it was holding back. I added them.

**Closing motion and parts staying aligned**
- `Standard/firelock-base.rsi/meta.json`: the `closing` animation's frame timings were 10× too short, so the door body snapped shut while its lights and panel kept animating at normal speed. I restored the same timings the glass firelock and the `opening` animation use.
- `Content.Client/Doors/DoorSystem.cs`: if the door closed while its opening animation was still playing, it played the *opening* animation again. It now plays the closing one.
- `SharedDoorSystem.OnPartialOpen` used the closing time instead of the opening time. The two values are equal for firelocks, so you won't see a difference there, but it was wrong.

The fixes I'm surest about are the air leak, the edge firelock's blocked side, the closing timings, the warnings staying on after opening, and the glass firelock's missing warning sprites. The alignment problem is my best guess: the sprite images themselves are all lined up, so I put it down to the lights and panel animating out of step with the door body.
